title: Change Brief
description: Structured extraction of a practitioner's prose brief (plus whatever else they gave us) into the A/M/T id spine. Stage 1 output. Mirrors rfp_brief.schema.json's shape: stable IDs are the spine the rest of the run maps against.

name.description: Organisation or team the change is happening in

slug.description: Used in the run workspace path comms/<org-slug>-<YYYYMMDD>/. Derived from name if not given.

name.description: Who the communications are sent as — a named leader, not a generic 'The Programme Team' unless that's genuinely the practitioner's choice

note.description: Why this sender — recognised authority for this audience is what makes an email get opened

change_summary.description: One or two sentences: what is changing. Feeds every channel's opening line.

audiences.description: Every distinct group the change lands on differently. IDs are A1, A2... The console's Step 02 audience segmentation is the primary source for this array.

name.description: The practitioner's own name for this group — payroll's own vocabulary, not a generic HR segment label

size.description: Roughly how many. A string like '~2,400' is fine; do not fabricate false precision

what_is_different.description: What changes for this group specifically, as distinct from every other audience

preferred_channels.description: Channel ids this audience actually reads/watches, if known. Informs Stage 2's channel selection but does not override coverage.

messages.description: IDs are M1, M2... Every message the change communications must land, including the six mandatory questions (what/who/why/when/action/help), what is explicitly NOT changing, and open unknowns the audience will ask about anyway.

kind.description: The six mandatory questions plus the two categories practitioners habitually omit: what is explicitly not changing, and open unknowns the audience will ask regardless of whether the brief answers them

text.description: The message content, in the sender's voice where possible

mandatory.description: False only for 'unknown' entries carried for transparency, not for delivery to every audience

audience_ids.description: Which audiences this message applies to. Empty/omitted means all audiences — Stage 5's coverage check treats it that way.

timeline.description: IDs are T1, T2... Every date practitioners tend to bury: go-live, cutover windows, training slots, the last day of the old process, review points.

date.description: ISO 8601 where a real date exists. A placeholder like 'TBC' belongs in open_questions instead, not here as a fabricated date.

confirmed.description: False means provisional. A false-confirmed date reaching a printed banner is exactly the failure Stage 5's cross-channel consistency check exists to catch.

open_questions.description: Every question the brief-interrogation left unanswered. An unanswered question becomes an entry here, never an invented answer in messages or timeline. Flows through to a visible [GAP] in the plan and report — see reference/brief-interrogation.md.

blocks.description: Which M/T/A ids can't be finalised until this is answered

sources.description: Every input the brief was built from — the console handoff, a prose brief document, a follow-up conversation
